title: What continuing education do Texas nurses need, including targeted CE?
seoTitle: Texas nursing CE and targeted CE
description: Texas BON Rule 216 as at November 2026: 20 contact hours or certification every two years, plus jurisprudence, older adult, forensic and trafficking CE.
shortAnswer: Texas nurses renewing an active license must complete 20 contact hours of continuing nursing education in their area of practice each two year licensing period, or achieve, maintain or renew a Texas Board of Nursing (BON) approved national nursing certification, under Board Rule 216.3. Targeted continuing education applies on top of the choice: jurisprudence and ethics for all nurses, plus older adult care, forensic evidence collection, human trafficking and prescribing topics for nurses whose practice triggers them.
keyTakeaways: Board Rule 216.3 requires 20 contact hours of continuing nursing education, or a board approved national certification, in the nurse's area of practice each licensing period.
Every nurse must complete 2 contact hours in nursing jurisprudence and nursing ethics before the end of every third two year licensing period, and certification cannot substitute.
Nurses providing direct patient care must complete an HHSC approved human trafficking prevention course every licensing period for renewals on or after September 1, 2020 (House Bill 2059).
Emergency room nurses need a one-time 2 hours in forensic evidence collection within two years of starting ER work, and nurses caring for older adults need 2 hours each period.

Records must be kept for three consecutive licensing periods or six years, and the forensic evidence collection record indefinitely; the board audits a random sample 90 days before each renewal month.
appliesTo: Licensed vocational nurses and registered nurses with an active Texas license
Advanced practice registered nurses, including those with prescriptive authority
Hospitals, emergency departments, long term care providers and staffing agencies employing Texas nurses
Nurses with Volunteer Retired Nurse Authorization, under reduced rules

sections.heading: What is the basic continuing competency requirement for Texas nurses?

blocks.text: For each renewal, a Texas nurse must either complete 20 contact hours of continuing nursing education (CNE) in their area of practice within the licensing period, or achieve, maintain or renew a board approved national nursing certification in that area. The Texas Board of Nursing sets this out in Board Rule 216.3 and summarizes it on its [continuing nursing education and competency page](https://www.bon.texas.gov/education_continuing_education.asp.html).

Rule 216.1 defines the terms. "Area of practice" is any activity, assignment or task in which the nurse used nursing knowledge, judgment or skills during the licensing period, or the most recent area of practice if the nurse has none. A "licensing period" follows the nurse's birth month and year and is 2 years after the first renewal; the initial period can run from 6 to 29 months.

CNE must come from a credentialing agency or provider the board recognizes, such as the American Nurses Credentialing Center, the American Association of Critical-Care Nurses, the American Association of Nurse Practitioners, the National League for Nursing, US colleges and universities, and other state boards of nursing. Hours earned in excess cannot be carried over to the next period.

sections.heading: What targeted CE do Texas nurses need, and who does it apply to?

blocks.text: Targeted continuing education is CE directed by statute and board rule at specific licensure levels or practice areas, as defined in Rule 216.1(21). Jurisprudence and ethics applies to every nurse; the rest depends on practice. Unless noted, targeted hours count toward the 20.

blocks.text: The board calculates that an APRN with prescriptive authority who prescribes controlled substances needs a total of 28 contact hours each licensing period. APRNs may use Category I continuing medical education for every targeted requirement except jurisprudence and ethics, which only CNE satisfies.

sections.heading: What must the Texas jurisprudence and ethics CE cover?

blocks.text: The course must cover the Texas Nursing Practice Act, the board's rules including Rule 217.11 (Standards of Nursing Practice), the board's position statements, principles of nursing ethics, and professional boundaries. Because the cycle is every third licensing period, a nurse can go two renewals without it, which makes it the requirement most often missed.

blocks.title: Certification is not a substitute
blocks.text: The board states: "Certification may not be used to fulfill the Nursing Jurisprudence and Nursing Ethics CNE requirement. All nurses (LVNs, RNs, and APRNs) must complete traditional CNE contact hours" for it, citing Board Rule 216.3(g).

sections.heading: Where do the human trafficking and forensic evidence requirements come from?

blocks.text: The human trafficking requirement comes from [House Bill 2059 (86th Legislature, 2019)](https://capitol.texas.gov/tlodocs/86R/billtext/html/HB02059F.htm), which added section 301.308 to the Texas Occupations Code. It requires a license holder who provides direct patient care to complete a human trafficking prevention course approved by the executive commissioner of the Health and Human Services Commission (HHSC), applying to nursing license renewals on or after September 1, 2020.

The board notes that in March 2025 HHSC revised its standards for reviewing human trafficking training courses and is reviewing all courses, including those previously approved, against them. Nurses should confirm a course is on the current HHSC list before relying on it. The multistate picture is in [human trafficking training requirements for healthcare](/regulations/human-trafficking-training-requirements-healthcare).

The forensic evidence collection requirement supports evidence collection under Government Code section 420.031, which governs the Attorney General approved evidence collection kit and protocol. Content may include documentation, history taking, sexual assault kit use, survivor symptoms and emotional and psychological support. A nurse who performs a forensic examination on a sexual assault survivor must complete basic forensic evidence collection training or equivalent education before performing the exam.

sections.heading: Are newly licensed Texas nurses exempt from CE?

blocks.text: Mostly. The board states that nurses are exempt from most continuing competency requirements for the first renewal after initial licensure if they renew on time. The only exception is the forensic evidence collection requirement, if the nurse works in an emergency room.

Similar exemptions apply for the period immediately after renewing a license delinquent for less than four years or reactivating one inactive for less than four years, again except forensic evidence collection. Nurses with Volunteer Retired Nurse Authorization need 10 contact hours (vocational or registered nurse level) or 20 hours (advanced practice level) in the two years before applying or renewing, and are exempt from targeted CE.

sections.heading: What records must Texas nurses keep, and how do BON audits work?

blocks.text: Nurses must keep original certificates of completion, contact hour certificates or official transcripts for at least three consecutive licensing periods or six years, citing Board Rules 216.7 and 216.3(d)(3). The forensic evidence collection record must be kept indefinitely, even after a change of employer.

Proof must show the program title, date and location, and the name of the credentialing agency; certification cards such as ACLS or PALS cards are not acceptable. The board selects a random sample of nurses 90 days before each renewal month, and an audited nurse cannot renew until proof is approved. A nurse who fails an audit is automatically audited in the next period, and failing to complete an audit or falsifying records is grounds for discipline. Employers can use the same file design described in [how to prepare training records for an audit](/guides/how-to-prepare-training-records-for-an-audit).

blocks.text: Multistate employers can compare these rules with [California](/regulations/california-nursing-continuing-education) and [Florida](/regulations/florida-nursing-continuing-education), which use flat hour totals and fixed topic cycles instead of practice based triggers.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry expresses each Texas targeted requirement as a rule attached to a practice setting or authority, such as emergency room assignment or prescriptive authority, so obligations follow the nurse when their role changes. Retention rules, including the indefinite forensic record, attach to the evidence itself. See [healthcare and life sciences](/industries/healthcare-life-sciences).

faqs.q: Can a national certification replace all Texas CE?
faqs.a: It replaces the 20 contact hours if the certification is board approved and in the nurse's area of practice. It does not replace jurisprudence and ethics, the human trafficking course, or the APRN pharmacotherapeutics and controlled substance hours, which must be completed as education.

faqs.q: Do Texas nurses send CE certificates with their renewal?
faqs.a: No. Nurses attest at renewal and submit documents only if selected for an audit, under Board Rule 216.9. Audits are completed online through a portal run by the board's contractor, and the nurse cannot renew until proof is reviewed and approved.

faqs.q: How long must Texas nurses keep CE records?
faqs.a: At least three consecutive licensing periods or six years. The certificate for the forensic evidence collection course must be kept indefinitely, even if the nurse changes employment.

faqs.q: Does the Texas jurisprudence and ethics CE apply every renewal?
faqs.a: No. It is due before the end of every third two year licensing period, for licensing periods that began on or after January 1, 2014. The board publishes examples showing how to work out the due period from birth month, birth year and licensure date.

factCheck.claim: Rule 216.3: 20 contact hours of CNE in area of practice within licensing period, or board approved national certification; definitions of contact hour 216.1(10), area of practice 216.1(4), licensing period 216.1(14) with initial 6 to 29 months; targeted CE definition 216.1(21); no carryover.

Jurisprudence and ethics: all nurses, 2 hours before the end of every third two year period (periods beginning on or after January 1, 2014); content list; certification not acceptable (216.3(g)); APRNs may not use CME.

Older adult 2 hours every period; forensic evidence collection 2 hours once within two years of ER employment, Government Code 420.031, record kept indefinitely; sexual assault examiner training before exam.

APRN prescriptive authority: 5 additional hours pharmacotherapeutics; 3 additional hours controlled substances; total 28; opioid PAA 2 hours annually (4 per period) for renewals on or after January 1, 2021 (HB 2454).

Human trafficking: nurses providing direct patient care, HHSC approved course every licensing period for renewals on or after September 1, 2020; HHSC revised standards March 2025 and reviewing all courses.
HB 2059 added Occupations Code 301.308 (direct patient care nurses complete HHSC approved course) and applies to nursing renewals on or after September 1, 2020; Act effective September 1, 2019.

Records kept three consecutive licensing periods or six years (216.7, 216.3(d)(3)); proof contents; random audit 90 days before renewal month; noncompliant nurses re-audited; first renewal exempt except forensic; VR nurse 10 or 20 hours and exempt from targeted CE.
